statement: Specification is version 1.2, dated 2026-08-29, pre-implementation, with status 'Final architecture'; implementation planning may begin from it.
The specification supersedes nothing and depends on Research I (category reconstruction), II (opportunity validation) and III (final gate) only as defect corpus and evidence base.
refines_or_supersedes: Research I, II, III (used as defect corpus/evidence base only, L6)

statement: The document does not revisit whether Entrybound should exist; conclusions about difficulty of displacing incumbents informed only the adoption architecture in §21.
refines_or_supersedes: Research I-III incumbent-displacement conclusions, confined to §21

statement: An adversarial architecture review of v1.0 found sixteen blocking issues; the most serious was an identity model inconsistent in five places, claiming both re-chunking-invariant logical identity and partial-read verification against one signed content digest.
refines_or_supersedes: v1.0 identity model corrected by v1.1 (§8.0, §9.6, §26.4, §26.5)
evidence_in_source: internal adversarial architecture review; details deferred to §26.4-§26.5
research_needed: Confirm all sixteen blocking issues are closed in the current spec and in code; trace each to §26.4/§26.5 entries.

statement: Version 1.1 replaced the single signed root with three signed roots (§8.0) and split signatures into two scopes (§9.6).
refines_or_supersedes: supersedes v1.0 single-root identity (§8.0, §9.6)

statement: Version 1.1 added six invariants, including the file-versus-directory prefix rule (§3.4 P6) required by the specification's own motivating vulnerability.
refines_or_supersedes: extends v1.0 invariant list

statement: Version 1.1 specifies the streaming chunk-framing mechanism that §4.6 had previously only asserted.
refines_or_supersedes: corrects v1.0 §4.6 assertion

statement: Version 1.1 downgraded several security and comparison claims to what the evidence supports; §26.4 and §26.5 list changes across two review passes.
refines_or_supersedes: narrows v1.0 security and comparison claims (§26.4, §26.5)
research_needed: Audit remaining superiority and security claims (§1.1, §11, §22, §23) against evidence to verify the downgrade was complete.

statement: The header labels the document version 1.2, but the revision note describes only the 1.0-to-1.1 changes; what changed in 1.2 is not stated in the front matter.
decision_needed: What are the version 1.2 deltas and where are they recorded (§26.4/§26.5)?

statement: Revision note says v1.1 adds six invariants, while §3.9 marks thirteen (I19-I31) as new, four of them promotions of C1/C2/T1/T2; per-revision provenance of each new invariant is unclear.
decision_needed: Which invariants were added in which revision, relative to the brief's starting list?

statement: §1.1 promises 'two separate identities so recompression does not break signatures', while the revision note says v1.1 introduced three signed roots (§8.0); the normative number of identities is inconsistent within the document.
research_needed: Reconcile §1.1 wording with §8.0 and any later identity-root additions.
decision_needed: How many identity roots are normative, and which ones do signatures cover?

statement: The specification reserves §24 for explicit non-goals and §25 for matters intentionally deferred to implementation design; §3-§4 point there for encoding details such as field widths and serialisation.
research_needed: Merge §24/§25 lists with this slice's open questions.

statement: Entrybound is defined as an archive system (semantic model, physical container, planning system, import/export adapters); the unit of delivery is eight components, not a file extension.
The Entrybound Archive Model (EAM), the canonical semantic model, is a core component.
The Entrybound Container Format (ECF), the native physical format, is a core component.
The native physical format uses the file extension `.eb` (detailed in §18).
research_needed: Check `.eb` for extension collisions with existing formats and OS associations; confirm media type plan in §18.

statement: The Compression Planner, performing content-directed transform and codec selection, is a core component.
Integrity, encryption, authentication and signing facilities are core components.
research_needed: External security review of the crypto design before v1.

statement: Import adapters for ZIP, tar-family and stream codecs are core components; 7z and RAR are not named among core import adapters.
decision_needed: Are 7z/RAR5 import adapters in v1 scope, given §1.1 positions Entrybound against 7z and RAR?

statement: Export adapters producing legacy artifacts, framed as a declared downgrade, are core components.
Inspection, verification, conversion and diagnostic tooling is a core component.
The CLI is core and comes first; library APIs follow, and language bindings are classified as ecosystem rather than core.
decision_needed: Is a stable public Rust library API part of v1, or internal until after the CLI ships?

statement: A public conformance corpus and a standalone verifier are promoted to core and must ship from v1; §19 and §20 justify why this is not optional.
research_needed: Define corpus coverage targets and build an independent minimal verifier to validate unique interpretation.

statement: One-sentence claim: a 2026 project gets from Entrybound everything ZIP, tar, 7z/RAR and modern container formats provide, plus properties none provide, without choosing which to give up.
research_needed: Capability and benchmark matrix against ZIP, tar, 7z, RAR5, zstd seekable, casync/borg-class containers; show no forced trade-off.

statement: Claim of ZIP parity: random access and per-entry codecs.
research_needed: Measure single-entry extraction latency and seek cost versus ZIP on large archives.

statement: Claim of tar parity for streaming: single-pass creation and reading.
research_needed: Demonstrate pipe-to-pipe pack and extract with bounded memory.

statement: Claim of tar parity for metadata fidelity.
research_needed: Round-trip fidelity matrix against GNU tar/bsdtar/pax on Linux, macOS, Windows.

statement: Claim of 7z/RAR parity: strong ratio and solid-grade cross-file compression.
research_needed: Benchmark compression ratio and speed against 7z LZMA2 solid and RAR5 on standard and real-world corpora, with random access retained.

statement: Claim of modern-container parity: chunk dedup, HTTP-range partial retrieval, and parallel decode.
research_needed: Benchmark dedup ratio, remote range fetch counts and decode scaling.

statement: Claim of unique properties: one semantic authority and structurally impossible traversal.
research_needed: Differential parsing across independent readers; extraction confinement tests including symlinks and Windows path normalisation.

statement: Claim of unique properties: authenticated encryption with an encrypted index, and hybrid post-quantum key encapsulation.
research_needed: External cryptographic review; confirm encrypted index hides names/sizes; assess hybrid PQ KEM maturity.

statement: Claim that separate identities mean recompression does not break signatures.
research_needed: Test that repack preserves logical-scope signatures and document which physical-scope signatures are invalidated.

statement: Claim of unique properties: declared resource bounds and an explicit statement of what was not preserved.
research_needed: Adversarial resource-exhaustion tests; FidelityReport completeness tests.

statement: The 'without having to choose' claim is in tension with known trade-offs: solid compression versus random access, encryption versus dedup and boundary leakage, and streaming versus declared budgets (conceded in §2.1(4)).
research_needed: Quantify each trade-off (ratio loss from bounded groups, dedup loss from leakage mitigation, streaming budget fallback).

statement: Every conforming `.eb` archive opened by every conforming reader yields exactly one interpretation of which entries exist, their names, kinds, bytes and metadata; there is no admissible-interpretation set.
research_needed: Conformance corpus plus differential testing between the main reader and an independent minimal reader.

statement: Ambiguity in the source of a converted archive (ZIP, tar) is recorded as data about the conversion (§14, §16), never as ambiguity in the resulting archive.
The unique-interpretation property is what the whole architecture is organised around; §11.4 concludes it is the property no incumbent provides.
research_needed: Verify with parser-differential evidence across incumbent formats (Research III corpus).

statement: The semantic model is authoritative; the container is an encoding of it and only one of possible serialisations; every question about an archive is answered by the model.

Two archives that serialise the same model are the same archive even if their bytes differ entirely, making recompression, re-chunking, re-encryption and layout conversion non-events rather than breaking changes.
research_needed: Define 'same model' precisely and test identity equality across repack variants.

statement: §3.1 places physical objects (Chunk, Segment, TransformPlan, Dictionary, CryptoEnvelope, Index) inside the model, yet §2.1(1) says re-chunking and re-encryption leave the model unchanged; the semantic-versus-physical partition of EAM objects is not delineated.
decision_needed: Which EAM objects are semantic (logical identity scope) and which are physical encoding, and which identity covers each?

statement: Re-chunking changes chunk_root, which flows into physical identity and the signed object; in what sense repack is a 'non-event' for physical-scope signatures is unresolved in this slice.
decision_needed: Which signature scope survives repack, and must repack strip or re-sign physical-scope signatures?

statement: Legacy formats are foreign encodings whose defects stop at the adapter boundary: ZIP LFH/CD duality, tar dialects, PAX override precedence, data descriptors, `..` components, duplicate names and trailing bytes have no EAM representation.
Legacy quirks are handled as observations made during import (§14) and resolutions recorded in a receipt (§16).
Backward compatibility is achieved by converting, never by accommodating legacy constructs in the native model.
research_needed: Check later documents (e.g., compat/preserve modes) for narrowing of 'never accommodating'.

statement: Every fact has exactly one authority; if a size, name, mode or digest can be read from two places the format is defective, because readers will eventually read different places.
Indexes exist but are caches, not authorities (§4.5).
Before the first payload byte is read, an archive declares its format version, required feature set, decoder memory requirement, its role, and where possible total logical bytes and entry count.
A reader unable to meet declared requirements fails immediately and states which requirement failed; it never discovers mid-decompression that it needed, e.g., a 2 GiB window.
A producer streaming from an unseekable source sets BudgetDeclared = false; the reader then falls back to caller policy and is explicitly told it did (§4.2).
refines_or_supersedes: narrows an unconditional capability-declaration promise
research_needed: Measure what budget fields a streaming producer can still declare (e.g., memory) versus totals.
decision_needed: What default caller-policy limits apply when BudgetDeclared = false?

statement: A streaming producer cannot know in advance which features (special files, holes, reconstructive transforms, chunk groups) its input needs, yet the required feature set must precede payload; BudgetDeclared = false covers only budgets.
decision_needed: May STREAM producers declare features conservatively, amend them in a trailer, or must undeclared features be errors?

statement: Archive 'role' is declared before payload, but role values and their effect on verification and extraction are not defined in §2-§3.
decision_needed: What archive roles exist (e.g., complete versus partial) and how does each change reader behaviour?

statement: Every archive records what it captured and what it could not capture.
Every extraction records what it restored and what it could not restore.
research_needed: Usability study of extraction loss reports.
decision_needed: What is the format and channel of the extraction report (CLI output, file, API object)?

statement: Every legacy conversion records what it dropped.
Design principle: an archive whose fidelity cannot be assessed is worse than one that is honestly lossy.
Entrybound refuses to be an accretion; the feature-refusal mechanism in §20 is designed first, because a format unable to refuse features eventually accepts all of them.
research_needed: Define and pilot the governance process that evaluates proposed features against the §3.9 invariant gate.

statement: ZIP's incoherence results not from bad decisions but from thirty years of individually reasonable additions with no mechanism for saying no.
research_needed: Historical analysis of APPNOTE revisions.

statement: Duplicated headers (ZIP local file header plus central directory) are rejected: two authorities are the root of the parser-differential class (§3.2, §11.4).
OS path strings as identity are rejected because of traversal, drive letters, separators, case and normalisation hazards (§3.4).
Streaming versus seeking is rejected as an either/or; both are claimed achievable in one design (§13).
research_needed: Demonstrate a single layout supporting single-pass write/read and indexed random access with bounded memory.

statement: Whole-archive codec choice is rejected: it prevents per-content optimisation and random access (§5).
Solid archives as an unbounded mode are rejected: random access collapses and corruption cascades (§7.5).
Unauthenticated encryption is rejected (§9.1).
7z, RAR5 and legacy ZIP encryption all ship unauthenticated encryption.
research_needed: Primary citations for 7z AES, RAR5 encryption/MAC design, ZipCrypto and WinZip AE; qualify wording if RAR5/AE provide partial authentication.

statement: Fail-open handling of unknown records is rejected because it makes silent misinterpretation a specification requirement (§20.2).
RAR5 mandates fail-open handling of unknown records.
research_needed: Cite the RAR5 technical note for unknown header/extra-record handling.

statement: Recovery records inside the archive are rejected: parity belongs outside, and the recovery parser is attack surface (§22.5).
research_needed: Validate external parity (e.g., PAR2) workflow usability and corruption-recovery coverage versus RAR recovery records.
decision_needed: How is external parity bound to and verified against an archive?

statement: Self-extracting executable prefixes are rejected as the canonical polyglot/prefix-confusion substrate (§11.4).
research_needed: Assess adoption cost for users who rely on SFX distribution.
decision_needed: Must readers reject any bytes before the preamble?

statement: In-band decompressor bytecode is rejected: it would solve longevity but costs every decoder a VM (§22.5).
research_needed: Establish the alternative longevity strategy (registry spec, standalone verifier, spec escrow) and its sufficiency.

statement: The EAM has twelve primary objects; everything else in the specification is a property of one of them.
The object tree names fifteen objects (Archive through Index), not twelve, and ChunkGroup is referenced by Chunk.group_ref, C1 and I29 but absent from the object list.
decision_needed: What is the normative object list, and is ChunkGroup a first-class model object?

statement: EntrySet is the authoritative set of Entries; each Entry holds LogicalPath, EntryKind, MetadataSet and an optional ContentRef.

ContentStore contains ContentObjects (immutable, content-addressed byte sequences), Chunks (unit of storage, transform, encryption, integrity) and Segments (contiguous chunk ranges, the unit of key derivation per §9.5).
Segments are the unit of key derivation, but who chooses segment boundaries, whether they are deterministic, and whether they affect physical identity or signatures is not stated in §3.
decision_needed: How are segment boundaries chosen and are they bound into identity?

statement: TransformPlan is described as per chunk-group, while every Chunk carries its own plan_ref; the granularity at which plans are assigned is ambiguous.
decision_needed: Are plans assigned per chunk or per chunk group, and may members of one group use different plans?

statement: CryptoEnvelope holds recipients, key commitment and suite identifiers.
SignatureSet holds author and attestation signatures over the root descriptor.
The Index is acceleration only: non-authoritative, reconstructible and optional (§4.5).
ArchiveDescriptor carries format version, three-tier feature bitmaps, declared resource budget, identity roots, layout declaration and path collision-class summary (§4.2).

An Entry is the sole authority for one archived object, with fields: path (LogicalPath unique within EntrySet), kind, content (ContentRef present iff kind carries content), metadata (MetadataSet), entry_id (digest over canonical form).
E1 single authority: no Entry field is representable anywhere else in the archive; no local copy, summary record or index field restates it.
The Index may cache entry facts, but a reader trusting a cached value without validating it against the Entry is non-conforming; the conformance corpus tests this (§19.3).
research_needed: Construct corpus cases with poisoned index caches and verify reader rejection.

statement: If every Index-cached fact must be validated against the authoritative Entry, what the Index accelerates for INDEXED and remote random access, and what validation cost is acceptable, is unresolved.
research_needed: Measure random-access latency and range-request counts with mandatory cache validation.

statement: E2 explicit identity: every Entry has an entry_id computed over its canonical serialised form; two Entries are the same iff entry_ids match, making entry dedup, diffing and incremental update well-defined.

entry_id is both a stored field and a digest over the Entry's canonical form; whether it covers path, all metadata (including items excluded from identity/v1), and encoding declarations, and whether readers must recompute it, is unspecified.
decision_needed: What exactly does entry_id cover, and is it stored or always derived?

statement: If entry_id covers the path, no two Entries in one archive can share it (P4), so 'entry-level dedup' can only be cross-archive; the intended scope of entry dedup, diff and incremental comparison is unstated.
decision_needed: Is entry identity meant for cross-archive comparison only, and should a path-independent content-and-metadata identity also exist?

statement: E3 content independence: an Entry names a ContentObject by digest and does not know how it is chunked, transformed, compressed or encrypted; changing those does not change the Entry.

Entries name ContentObjects by logical digest, but a ContentObject also carries chunk_root and a chunk list; whether one archive may hold two ContentObjects with equal logical_digest but different chunkings, and which one an Entry references, is unspecified.
decision_needed: Is ContentObject unique per logical_digest within an archive?

statement: EntryKind is exactly: Directory, File, Symlink, Fifo, Socket, BlockDevice, CharDevice.
Fifo entries require the `special-files` feature; Socket entries are marked gated (the feature name is given only for Fifo).
BlockDevice and CharDevice entries are gated and require a privileged extraction policy.
decision_needed: What is the privileged extraction policy, its default, and how is it opted into?

statement: Socket entries are gated but no restoration semantics are given (sockets generally cannot be meaningfully recreated), and where device major/minor numbers live is not stated in §3.
decision_needed: Should Socket be representable at all, and what does extraction do with it?

statement: EntryKind has no representation for Windows reparse points/junctions, overlay or OCI whiteouts, or other platform object kinds; whether these are metadata, unrepresentable, or future kinds, and how unknown kinds are handled under I12, is not stated.
decision_needed: How are non-POSIX filesystem object kinds and future EntryKinds represented?

statement: Hardlink is not an EntryKind: two Entries naming the same ContentObject are content-sharing, the complete structural fact; source hard-linking is a metadata assertion `posix.hardlink_group`.
Hardlink-before-target is not representable because there is no ordering relationship (unlike GNU tar typeflag 1, which requires the target first).
A symlink's content is its target path; hardlink-to-symlink ambiguity is said to disappear because sharing it is ordinary content sharing.
refines_or_supersedes: qualified by §3.3a item 3 (L190)

statement: Dedup and hardlinks unify: the mechanism storing one copy of two identical files is the mechanism that represents a hard link.
Whether to recreate hard links, copy content, or reflink is an extraction policy decision (§11.6), not an archive decision.

Because identical unrelated files also share a ContentObject, an extractor recreating hard links from content sharing alone would link independent files; whether link recreation must be driven only by posix.hardlink_group is not stated.
decision_needed: Must hard-link recreation require posix.hardlink_group membership rather than content equality?

statement: Symlink targets are stored as content bytes with no EncodingDeclaration and are not LogicalPaths, so P1-P8 do not govern them; target encoding, separators, absolute or `..` targets, and cross-platform restoration are unspecified here.
research_needed: Adversarial symlink-escape extraction tests on Linux, macOS and Windows.
decision_needed: What validation and extraction policy applies to symlink targets?

statement: Content equality is not inode identity; the model must handle three resulting cases explicitly rather than absorb them.
A hardlinked tree and a tree of identical copies have the same identity/v1 LAI, because posix.hardlink_group is metadata excluded from the default profile; identity/strict-v1 includes it (§8.3).

Since posix.hardlink_group participates in identity/strict-v1, group identifiers must be assigned canonically (independent of inode numbers and traversal order) for strict identity to be deterministic; no assignment rule appears in §3.
decision_needed: What canonical rule assigns hardlink group identifiers?

statement: Hardlinked special files (FIFOs, sockets, device nodes) carry no ContentRef, so they are represented by posix.hardlink_group alone, and exporting them to a format with a link kind is lossy (§15.2).

Two symlinks with the same target are indistinguishable from two hardlinks to one symlink inode except via posix.hardlink_group and extraction policy; §11.2's 'not representable' covers structural hazards (ordering, target-before-link, link-to-link), not inode-identity fidelity.
refines_or_supersedes: narrows §3.3 L180 consequence and §11.2 'not representable' booking

statement: Tar hardlink import resolves in one pass using a deferred-resolution table: the link records an unresolved reference and its Entry is completed once the target's ContentObject digest is known.
The memory bound of the deferred-resolution table (many unresolved links, adversarial inputs) and its interaction with declared budgets and bounded staging during streaming import are not addressed.
research_needed: Measure worst-case table growth on adversarial tar inputs; define a caller-policy cap.

statement: For hardlink import, the first occurrence wins for the content; a link whose target never appears is an Irreconcilable conflict (§14.2).

'First occurrence wins' is ambiguous when the link target name appears several times in a tar stream, or when a hardlink entry itself carries data (as some pax writers allow) that differs from the target.
decision_needed: How are repeated targets and data-bearing hardlink entries resolved and classified?

statement: A tar hardlink to a symlink resolves to the symlink's ContentObject, and the disambiguation is recorded.
Directory entries exist explicitly and are never inferred from paths; empty directories are allowed; a directory entry never carries content.
Research III corpus case EB-Z025: a ZIP entry whose name ends in `/` but carries bytes; EAM makes it unrepresentable.
A LogicalPath is an ordered, non-empty sequence of PathComponents, not a string.
A PathComponent is a non-empty octet string excluding 0x00 and 0x2F, plus an EncodingDeclaration: utf8, utf8-nfc, utf8-nfd, utf16le, opaque-bytes, or legacy(charset).
Excluding bytes 0x00 and 0x2F conflicts with the utf16le declaration: UTF-16LE encodes ASCII names with 0x00 bytes and many code units contain 0x2F, and P7's own example `2E 00 2E 00` contains 0x00.
decision_needed: Drop utf16le, transcode on import, or define byte exclusions on decoded code points instead?

statement: Whether writers and readers must validate that component bytes are well-formed under the declared encoding (valid UTF-8, genuinely NFC/NFD), under which Unicode version, and what happens on mismatch, is unspecified.
research_needed: Unicode-version stability of normalisation checks; security of lenient decoders (e.g., overlong UTF-8 dots).
decision_needed: Is declared-encoding well-formedness normative and fail-closed?

statement: legacy(charset) has no defined charset naming registry or mapping tables (vendor variants differ), yet P7 validity depends on decoding under the declared encoding.
decision_needed: Which charset names and mapping tables are normative for legacy(charset)?

statement: Whether EncodingDeclaration participates in entry_id and LAI is not stated; if it does, importer charset heuristics (e.g., ZIP CP437 versus UTF-8 flag) change the logical identity of byte-identical names.
decision_needed: Does the declared encoding contribute to entry identity and LAI?

statement: Canonical entry order: length-prefix each component's bytes, concatenate, and compare as unsigned octet strings; length-prefixing makes the order total and distinguishes [a, b] from [ab].
EncodingDeclaration does not participate in ordering; two entries with identical component bytes are illegal under P4 regardless of declared encodings.
Canonical order is normative: it determines the manifest Merkle root, hence LAI, hence every signature.

The length-prefix encoding (fixed width, endianness, or varint) changes the resulting order for long components, but field widths and serialisation are deferred (§4, §25) while the order is normative for LAI.
decision_needed: Which length-prefix encoding defines canonical order, and must it be frozen before LAI is frozen?

statement: A single-pass STREAM producer must yield a manifest in canonical order with all P6 ancestors present; whether this requires buffering and sorting every path (memory beyond budgets for very large trees) is not addressed in §3.
research_needed: Memory and time scaling of manifest sorting for 10^7-10^8 entries; external sort feasibility.

statement: P1 no traversal: `..` and `.` are not PathComponents; no byte sequence means 'parent'.

Traversal is claimed unwritable rather than defended against; this holds for LogicalPaths, but extraction can still escape through symlink targets, pre-existing on-disk links, or Windows path normalisation.
research_needed: Cross-platform extraction confinement tests with adversarial names, symlinks and pre-existing directory links.

statement: P2: no absolute paths and no roots: no leading separator, drive letter, UNC prefix, or volume GUID.
Every path is relative to an extraction root supplied by the caller.
P3: there is no separator in the model; backslash-versus-slash confusion (EB-Z014) cannot occur, and a component containing 0x2F is invalid.
A legacy name like `a/b` in a single ZIP name field either splits into two components or fails import under strict mode, and the receipt records which occurred.
decision_needed: What is the non-strict default, and how are the resulting parent Directory entries synthesised?

statement: P4: no two Entries may have equal LogicalPaths, equality being byte equality of the component sequence; duplicate-name selection becomes unrepresentable.
Duplicate-name selection is an exploited class: Android Master Key (CVE-2013-4787) and Research III case EB-Z001.
evidence_in_source: primary CVE citation and Research III corpus case

statement: P6: every proper prefix of each Entry's LogicalPath must exist as an Entry of kind Directory; an archive containing [a, b] must contain [a] as a Directory.
refines_or_supersedes: added in v1.1 (Revision note L10)

statement: P6 closes the §11.4 motivating defect (one name denoting both file and directory, resolved differently by two components of one product), which P4 alone does not forbid.
research_needed: Conformance corpus cases with file/directory name conflicts.

statement: There are no implicit directories; an extractor never invents a directory with an invented mode.

Legacy ZIP and tar inputs often omit parent directory entries; P6 forces the importer to synthesise Directory entries, but their metadata/mode, whether they are flagged in the receipt or FidelityReport, and classification of file-versus-directory conflicts are unspecified here.
decision_needed: What metadata do synthesised directories get, and how are they recorded?

statement: P6 requires every ancestor to be a Directory, making paths through a Symlink entry unrepresentable; whether this is intended, and that extractors must still defend against on-disk links outside the archive, is not stated.
P7: a component is invalid if its bytes, decoded under the declared encoding, are `.` or `..`; raw-byte checks are insufficient (UTF-16 `..` is 2E 00 2E 00); normative for writers and readers.
How P7 applies to opaque-bytes components, and whether it covers target-equivalent forms (Windows trailing dots/spaces such as '... ' collapsing, fullwidth dots after normalisation), is unspecified.
research_needed: Enumerate Win32/NT, macOS and Linux name canonicalisations that can yield parent/current references.

statement: P8: target-hostile bytes (0x5C and ':' on Windows, control bytes) are legal in the archive, so POSIX trees containing them can be archived faithfully.
An extractor targeting a platform where component bytes are structurally meaningful must refuse or apply a declared renaming policy.
decision_needed: Which renaming policies are defined, and what is the default?

statement: The ArchiveDescriptor summarises which path hostility classes are present so a caller can refuse before extracting.
decision_needed: What is the enumerated set of hostility classes?

statement: Deliberate narrowing: separator confusion is eliminated between archive and reader (paths are sequences) but only managed between reader and target filesystem, whose rules cannot be legislated away.
refines_or_supersedes: narrows an earlier, stronger claim that separator confusion was eliminated

statement: P5: byte-distinct paths that would collide on a target (case-fold, NFC/NFD, Windows reserved names, trailing dot/space, Unicode confusables) are legal in the archive, which stores exact bytes.
The extractor must detect the collision class for its target and refuse or apply a declared policy; writers SHOULD warn about collisions.
Collisions are neither normalised at write time (destroys information) nor refused at write time (would make faithful Linux archival impossible).
ArchiveDescriptor carries a `path.collision_classes` summary so a reader knows before extraction that, e.g., a case-collision pair exists.

Collision detection is target- and version-dependent (Unicode case folding and normalisation versions, NTFS per-volume upcase tables, APFS/HFS+ rules, per-directory case sensitivity), so a writer-computed summary cannot anticipate every target.
research_needed: Survey filesystem collision rules and their versioning; define deterministic reference tables.
decision_needed: Which collision classes and reference tables are normative for the summary and for extractors?

statement: The collision-class and hostility-class summaries restate facts derivable from Entries; how they reconcile with single authority, whether readers must validate them, and whether a false summary is corruption, is unspecified.
decision_needed: Are descriptor path summaries advisory caches or validated authorities?

statement: Unicode confusables are listed among collision classes the extractor must detect, but confusables do not collide on filesystems and confusable data (UTS #39) is large and version-dependent.
decision_needed: Is confusable detection mandatory, advisory, or out of scope for extractors?

statement: ContentObject = logical_digest (over plaintext, chunking-independent), chunk_root (Merkle root over chunk list, chunking-dependent), and an ordered chunk list that may be empty for zero-length content.
Chunk = chunk_id (digest over plaintext chunk bytes), logical_len, plan_ref (TransformPlanID), and optional group_ref (ChunkGroupID).
There is no logical_size field: a ContentObject's logical size is exactly the sum of its chunks' logical_len values, with no exceptions or side terms (enforcing I19).
The O(1) per-entry budget check a size field would serve is instead provided by the descriptor's max_single_entry_logical_bytes (§4.2).
decision_needed: What default and maximum values apply to max_single_entry_logical_bytes?

statement: Holes are chunks: a registered `hole` TransformPlan has a logical_len, produces that many zero bytes and stores no bytes; ContentObjects have no sparse map, offset resolution is uniform, and chunk_root covers holes.
Modelling holes as chunks means the unbounded sparse-map allocation class (I20) cannot arise, because holes are bounded by the same chunk-count budget as other chunks.
research_needed: Adversarial tests with extreme sparse inputs against chunk-count budgets.

statement: No maximum logical_len is given for hole chunks: one huge hole chunk bypasses chunk-count bounds on output size (bounded only per entry), tiny hole chunks inflate counts, and hashing plaintext zeros for chunk_id is costly unless special-cased.
decision_needed: What bounds hole chunk logical_len, and is the hole chunk_id computed or special-cased?

statement: In encrypted archives, hole chunks storing no bytes, and visible chunk logical_len values, may reveal sparse geometry and plaintext structure, in tension with I24.
research_needed: Leakage analysis of hole and chunk-length visibility under encryption; padding options.

statement: Source filesystem hole geometry, being advisory and non-deterministic (§10.7), is preserved separately as `posix.sparse_hint` metadata that participates in nothing.
decision_needed: Does 'participates in nothing' exclude sparse_hint from strict identity profiles, signatures and FidelityReport?

statement: There is no stored_len field: a chunk's physical length is declared exactly once, in its chunk frame (§4.6); the manifest carries logical facts and the frame physical ones.

With physical lengths only in chunk frames and the Index non-authoritative, how an INDEXED or HTTP-range reader locates a chunk's physical offset without a second authority or frame scanning is unresolved in §3 (§4.5-§4.6).
research_needed: Cross-check §4.5-§4.6 design; measure range requests needed to locate a chunk cold.

statement: Group membership is declared in one direction only: Chunk.group_ref is the authority; a ChunkGroup does not enumerate its members, and the member list is derived.
Decoding a chunk-group member needs its lookback predecessors, but membership is derivable only by scanning chunks' group_ref; the random-access cost of deriving group members is not addressed.
research_needed: Measure member-derivation cost for remote random reads of grouped chunks.

statement: logical_digest is over plaintext bytes, invariant under re-chunking; it is what an Entry names (E3) and what flows into LAI.
refines_or_supersedes: corrects earlier draft that conflated digests (L261)

statement: chunk_root is a Merkle root over the chunk list that changes whenever chunking changes; it flows into physical identity and the signed object as a separate field (§8.3, §9.6), giving remote range readers an authenticated root.
refines_or_supersedes: corrects earlier draft (L261)

statement: A single digest cannot be both re-chunking-invariant and a verification root for partial reads; an earlier draft conflated them and claimed mutually exclusive properties.
refines_or_supersedes: corrects v1.0 draft identity model

statement: Files reference ContentObjects; ContentObjects reference Chunks; Chunks are the unit of everything physical.
Rejected: files referencing chunks directly, since that loses single-comparison content equality needed for entry dedup, diffing and hardlink unification.
Rejected: files as Merkle roots; a Merkle tree is a verification structure over the chunk list (built per §8.6), while the chunk list remains the model object.
Offset-to-chunk resolution must be O(1); with only per-chunk logical_len and no declared offsets (I19), this needs a derived prefix-sum structure or else is O(log n) search.
research_needed: Specify the offset-resolution structure and its memory cost; benchmark for million-chunk objects.

statement: Rejected: content-defined chunks only; some content (small files, incompressible blobs) is better stored as one chunk, so chunking is a planner decision (§5, §7), not a model constraint.
C1: given the TransformPlan set and dictionaries, any chunk is decodable without decoding any other chunk; chunk groups (§7.5) relax this only in a declared, bounded way when the archive says so.
C2: chunk_id and content digest are computed over uncompressed, unencrypted bytes, so identity survives recompression and a logical identity can be defined.
C2 refers to a `digest` field, while the ContentObject field is named logical_digest; field naming drifts within §3.5.

Plaintext-addressed chunk_id and logical_digest in encrypted archives permit confirmation-of-file attacks if visible without keys; whether these digests are keyed or only exist inside encrypted structures is not stated in §3.
research_needed: Security review of digest exposure in encrypted archives; consider keyed digests.
decision_needed: Are content and chunk digests keyed or encrypted in encrypted archives?

statement: The digest algorithm and Merkle construction for ContentDigest, ChunkDigest, ChunkTreeRoot and EntryIdentity, including the root of an empty chunk list, are not specified in §3.
research_needed: Cross-check §8 for algorithm choice and domain separation.

statement: Whether a zero-length File carries a ContentRef with an empty chunk list or no ContentRef, given 'present iff kind carries content', is not pinned down.
decision_needed: Canonical representation of zero-length file content?

statement: TransformPlan = plan_id, ordered reversible transforms, codec, codec_params, optional dictionary, and decode_req (window, memory, and whether a VM or large state is needed).
decode_req records whether a VM is needed, yet §2.3 rejects in-band decompressor bytecode for costing decoders a VM; which registered codecs or transforms may require a VM or large state is unclear.
decision_needed: Are any VM-requiring codecs or transforms admissible in the registry?

statement: A TransformStep is a named, registered, reversible operation carrying needed reconstruction side-data; examples: executable filter, delta, byte-shuffle, deflate reconstruction (preflate class), JPEG entropy re-coder (Lepton class), float-field split (ZipNN class).
decision_needed: Which transforms are in the v1 registry?

statement: Reconstructive transforms must reconstruct bit-exactly across independent decoder implementations and versions, which requires a normative specification per transform; the writer's round-trip only proves its own decoder.
research_needed: Cross-implementation reproducibility of preflate/Lepton-class reconstruction; availability of normative specs.

statement: A Dictionary is a first-class archive object with an ID, stored once and referenced by many plans.
Per-file embedded dictionaries are the known failure mode by which dictionary compression loses to solid compression; shared first-class dictionaries are the difference.
research_needed: Benchmark shared-dictionary versus per-file-dictionary versus solid compression on small-file corpora.

statement: Random-access and remote readers must fetch dictionaries to decode any chunk (C1); dictionary size budgets, encryption, and fetch cost are not declared in §3.
research_needed: Measure dictionary fetch overhead for remote single-entry reads.

statement: T1 plans are data: a decoder implements the registry of transforms and codecs, not the planner; the archive fully determines its own decoding.
A 2026 decoder decodes a 2046 archive if and only if it implements the declared features, which it can determine before allocating anything (§4.8).
research_needed: Feature-negotiation tests with synthetic future-feature archives; decoder longevity strategy.

statement: T2: no predictive transform (preflate, Lepton, JXL lossless-JPEG) enters an archive unless the writer performed a full round-trip confirming byte-exact reconstruction; §5.6 makes this normative.
libjxl cannot reliably recompress JPEGs produced by jpegli.
evidence_in_source: asserted as a measured failure mode; no citation in slice
research_needed: Reproduce with current libjxl on a jpegli-produced corpus.

statement: preflate's correction stream degrades (grows) rather than failing when reconstruction diverges.
evidence_in_source: asserted as a measured failure mode; no citation in slice
research_needed: Measure correction-stream growth across deflate encoders (zlib levels, zopfli, libdeflate, 7-Zip).

statement: Write-time verification converts an unbounded correctness risk into a bounded cost; the throughput and memory cost is not quantified.
research_needed: Benchmark pack throughput with and without round-trip verification.

statement: T2's heading says every transform is verified at write time, but its body and I31 restrict verification to predictive/reconstructive transforms; whether ordinary codecs and structural filters are also round-trip verified is unclear.
decision_needed: Is write-time round-trip verification required for all transforms and codecs or only reconstructive ones?

statement: A MetadataSet is a set of typed, namespaced items, each carrying a criticality bit and a restorability class, not a bag of anonymous key-value extra fields (§10).
Handling of an unknown metadata item with the criticality bit set is unspecified: fail at open, fail when extracting that entry, or fail only when restoring that item.
decision_needed: At what point does an unknown critical metadata item cause failure?

statement: FidelityReport is a first-class, in-band, typed record of what could not be captured (§10.9).
ConversionRecord (provenance) is present only on archives produced by import (§16).
Because ConversionRecord exists only for imports, whether native-to-native repack, transcode, merge or re-encryption produce any provenance record is unspecified.
decision_needed: Do native repack operations record provenance, and how do chained receipts work?

statement: §3.9 consolidates the invariant list, marking departures from the brief's starting list; I1-I18 derive from the brief and I19-I31 are new.
refines_or_supersedes: extends the design brief's starting invariant list

statement: I1: One semantic authority exists for every fact.
I2: No duplicated semantic headers.
I3: Logical paths are unique under byte equality.
I4: Paths are structural sequences, not OS path strings.
I5: `..` and `.` are not representable.
I6: Duplicate entries are not representable.
I7: Every entry has an explicit identity digest.
I8: Compression is independent of logical archive identity.
I9: Encryption is independent of logical archive identity.
I10: Indexes are acceleration structures, never authorities, and are reconstructible.
I11: Metadata is typed, namespaced, and explicitly scoped.
I12: Unknown critical features fail closed; unknown optional features are ignored but authenticated.
I13: No silent metadata loss; loss is a typed in-band record.
I15: Archive interpretation is deterministic and unique.
I16: Extraction policy is separate from archive semantics and cannot be overridden by the archive.
I18: Legacy ambiguity is preserved and surfaced at import, never silently normalised.
I19: New: every size, offset and count is declared exactly once.
refines_or_supersedes: departure from the brief's starting invariant list

statement: I20: New: no unbounded list is parsed from a header; every repeated structure has a declared, bounded count validated against the descriptor.
refines_or_supersedes: departure from the brief's starting invariant list

statement: I21: New: truncation is distinguishable from corruption, and both from unsupported features.
refines_or_supersedes: departure from the brief's starting invariant list

statement: I22: New: a published identity is a digest over a descriptor that binds parameters, never a bare Merkle root.
refines_or_supersedes: departure from the brief's starting invariant list

statement: I23: New: hard links are content sharing, not a link kind.
refines_or_supersedes: departure from the brief's starting invariant list

statement: I24: New: physical chunk boundaries must not leak plaintext structure in encrypted archives.
refines_or_supersedes: departure from the brief's starting invariant list

statement: I25: New: a reader that cannot verify a result must report it as unverified and never present unverified output as verified.
refines_or_supersedes: departure from the brief's starting invariant list

statement: I26: New: no path is a proper prefix of another unless the prefix entry is a Directory, and every ancestor exists as an explicit Directory entry (P6).
refines_or_supersedes: promotes §3.4 P6 into invariant list

statement: I27: New: `.` and `..` are excluded under every declared encoding, not merely as raw bytes (P7).
refines_or_supersedes: promotes §3.4 P7 into invariant list

statement: I28: New (was C2): content addressing is over plaintext, so logical identity (LAI) is independent of compression, chunking and encryption; PCR is deliberately chunking-dependent (§8.0).
refines_or_supersedes: promotes §3.5 C2 (L271)

statement: I29: New (was C1): every chunk is independently decodable unless it belongs to a chunk group whose lookback is declared.
refines_or_supersedes: promotes §3.5 C1 (L269)

statement: I30: New (was T1): transform plans are data; a decoder implements the registry, never the planner.
refines_or_supersedes: promotes §3.6 T1 (L290)

statement: I31: New (was T2): no reconstructive transform enters an archive without a verified byte-exact round-trip.
refines_or_supersedes: promotes §3.6 T2 (L292); narrows T2 wording to reconstructive transforms

statement: I14 (part 1): no silent lossy conversion.
I14 (part 2): no lossy transforms at all may be used inside an archive (§6.5).

I17: resource limits are declared before payload and validated before allocation, or the archive declares it cannot (BudgetDeclared = false), in which case the reader enforces caller policy alone and reports that it did.
I6 (duplicate entries not representable) is not distinguished from I3 (unique paths); whether 'duplicate entry' means anything beyond duplicate path is unstated.

I19 requires each count and size be declared exactly once, yet §2.1(4) has the descriptor declare total logical bytes and entry count, and I20 validates structure counts against the descriptor; these appear to declare derivable facts twice.
decision_needed: Are descriptor totals bounds (limits) rather than facts, and how are mismatches with actual structures classified?

statement: 'Unknown optional features are ignored but authenticated': what authenticates them in archives with no signature or encryption, and whether identity digests must cover them, is not stated.
decision_needed: What mechanism authenticates ignored optional features in unsigned, unencrypted archives?

statement: Distinguishing truncation from corruption requires a mandatory end commitment; how a STREAM reader tells an archive cut at a frame boundary from a complete one is not specified in §3.
research_needed: Truncation-at-every-offset tests against the reference reader.

statement: Streaming extraction emits bytes before end-of-archive roots or signatures can be checked; how per-file versus whole-archive 'unverified' status is reported, and whether output is withheld, is unresolved in §3.
decision_needed: Does streaming extraction stage output until verification, or mark it unverified?

statement: I24 forbids chunk-boundary leakage in encrypted archives, but the mitigation (keyed CDC, padding, fixed-size chunking) and its dedup and ratio cost are not specified in §3.
research_needed: Evaluate mitigations against the 2025 CDC attack literature and measure dedup loss.
decision_needed: Which boundary-leakage mitigation is mandatory for encrypted archives?

statement: The invariant list, used as the feature gate (§23.5), omits P2 (no roots), P5 (collisions detected, not normalised), P8 (hostile bytes legal, extractor handles), directory-carries-no-content, and hole semantics.
decision_needed: Should the omitted model rules be promoted into the gating invariant list?

statement: §23.5 makes the invariant list the gate for every future feature; I28-I31 were promoted because a gate omitting 'transforms must be verified' is not a gate.
refines_or_supersedes: cross-reference §23.5

statement: I26 and I27 close the file-versus-directory and encoding-dependent traversal gaps that P4 and P1 alone leave open.
refines_or_supersedes: refines P1/P4 (§3.4)

statement: Origin of I19: PyPI's accepted test corpus contains an archive whose declared size and actual stream disagree; six implementations give five different answers, and both readings pass CRC.
evidence_in_source: Research III finding (cited, not reproduced in slice)
research_needed: Re-run the six-implementation differential and record the Research III case identifier.

statement: Origin of I20: the unbounded-allocation class found in tar sparse-map parsing.
evidence_in_source: Research finding referenced; no specific citation in slice
research_needed: Cite the concrete tar sparse-map allocation vulnerabilities.

statement: Origin of I21: a generalisation of the xz flags-CRC refinement.
evidence_in_source: reference to xz format design; no citation in slice

statement: Origin of I22: the fs-verity descriptor lesson (publish a digest over a parameter-binding descriptor, not a bare Merkle root).
evidence_in_source: reference to fs-verity design; no citation in slice

statement: Origin of I24: the 2025 content-defined-chunking attack literature, described as the single input most likely missed by designers unfamiliar with that work (§7.6).
